post.description:
Clone-and-publish a bespoke flat price at catalog and, by default, re-pin the
organization's live subscription to it.

**`effective`, decided by subscription's own existing change-plan rule (`_change_plan`,
ADR-0005 addendum §4) — this endpoint never overrides it:**

* `"now"` — the subscription is on the new price immediately: it was trialling (no charge),
  or it was `active` and the new price is a paid *upgrade* (charged now, prorated for the
  rest of the period).
* `"next_period"` — the subscription was `active` and the new price is a paid *downgrade*:
  subscription's existing scheduled-change mechanism applies it at `current_period_end`, so
  as not to take back time already paid for.
* `"not_subscribed"` — the organization has no subscription for this product,
  `apply_to_subscription` was `false`, or the live subscription is `past_due`, `suspended` or
  `cancelled` (subscription refuses a change-plan outright in those states — there is no
  fourth `effective` value for that refusal, so it is folded into this one; the bespoke price
  is still created and published regardless).

`Idempotency-Key` is an optional header; a retried request with the same key and the same
body returns the first attempt's result rather than repeating the catalog/subscription calls.
The same key with a different body is a 409.

parameters.description: Optional, at most 255 characters. A retried request with the same key and the same body returns the first attempt's result instead of repeating the catalog/subscription calls; the same key with a different body is a 409.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional, at most 255 characters. A retried request with the same key and the same body returns the first attempt's result instead of repeating the catalog/subscription calls; the same key with a different body is a 409.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

post.summary: Set a client's price for a product — a bespoke plan version, optionally applied now

post.description:
Switch the organization's subscription for `product_key` to `plan_version_id`.

**When it takes effect is decided by the server, never asked for** (ADR-0029): a trial switches
now and free; a paying subscription switches at its **next billing period** (`effective:
"next_period"`, landing at `effective_at`); an equal-price change applies now at no charge. For
a customer who should get a new plan sooner, grant comp credit instead.

`reason` (1-500 characters) is required and recorded on the audit trail — never on the
subscription's event, which the customer org's own notification templates can render;
`expected` is the state the preview returned, compared under subscription's lock (409
`state_changed`). The target must be one catalog offers this organization *now* (the picker's
set, re-read here): a version superseded by a newer one, or of a retired plan, is 422
`not_offerable` — except a withdrawal back to the pin the subscription is on.
Errors carry a stable `errors[0].code`: 404 `no_subscription` / `not_found`; 409
`state_changed`, `billing_catching_up`, `request_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reused`; 422
`state`, `cadence`, `currency`, `already_pinned`, `product_mismatch`, `not_published`,
`not_offerable`, `reserved_reason`, `bundle`; 503 `catalog_unavailable` — this request changed
nothing; 503 `outcome_unknown` — the change may or may not have been made: refresh, or repeat
the same request, which reconciles.

parameters.description: Required, 8-255 characters. A claim row keyed on it is written before the subscription is called: a retry with the same key and body returns the recorded result without a second change; the same key with a different body is a 409; two concurrent requests with one key make one change.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Required, 8-255 characters. A claim row keyed on it is written before the subscription is called: a retry with the same key and body returns the recorded result without a second change; the same key with a different body is a 409; two concurrent requests with one key make one change.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

post.summary: Switch a subscription's plan — a trial now, a paying subscription at its next period

post.description:
The confirm screen's server-computed preview: direction, when it lands, what it replaces,
the products it adds or removes — and the `expected` state to send back on the confirm. A
refusal (a past_due subscription, a different currency or cadence, a version catalog no longer
offers this organization — `not_offerable`) is part of the answer. Nothing is written, claimed
or locked; a failure says so (503 `preview_unavailable`, never `outcome_unknown`).

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
